name: Briar Barrett
life: “I still remember repainting a line that was hard to see only in drizzle.” People around the brick passage off the shop row know Briar by a small Sunday habit. Briar takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I paint the edge line. The driver pointed out the place where the existing paint disappears in reflected light.
appearance: Briar has close-cropped dark curls, an aquiline nose and a square chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a striped cotton shirt. It usually goes with one cuff folded back twice. When somebody else has the floor, Briar presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Briar loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To repaint the section that vanishes under reflection.
family: Cole Dunn is Briar’s cousin raised in the same household. Briar leaves the first voice message. Cole calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A call heard twice*, Cole says, “I typed the reply and changed saved you to stayed with you.”
connections: Jacob Nelson. The instructor and painter compare the view through a moving windscreen.

reactions.situation: A friend insists the return journey must happen that night
reactions.response: Briar asks the learner when they want to try again, leaving the friend's timetable out of it.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Briar offers to walk to the next staffed place together, at the stranger's pace, to ask about another ride.

reactions.situation: If a stranger asks to hear a private story
reactions.response: Briar offers one about their own embarrassment instead.
